records.title: 2026 Victorian Election Pendulum

structuralSignals: Traditional two-party pendulums are less reliable in a three-party contest.
One Nation strength is expected to be greater outside metropolitan Melbourne and may threaten both Coalition and safe Labor seats.
Green preference concentration can allow Labor to retain more seats than primary-vote comparisons imply.
Coalition losses to One Nation or independents raise the number of Labor gains required for a Coalition majority.

records.notes: A structural comparator rather than a poll observation. Preference benchmarks and geographic patterns are useful candidates for sensitivity testing, but should not be imported as Victorian parameters without validation.
